Situation1: They occasionally participate in family traditions during holidays and gatherings.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Story: I was sitting in the living room, surrounded by the familiar warmth of my family as we prepared for our annual holiday dinner. My parents had always emphasized the importance of these gatherings, reminding me that upholding our traditions was a way of honoring our roots. Just as my mother called me to help set the table, my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my closest friend, his voice shaky with panic. He was on his way to the airport for a long-awaited trip, but he thought he’d left his passport at home. He begged me to check his apartment and, if I found it, rush it to him before his flight. I could hear the desperation in his voice—he had no one else to call. My parents expected me to be present, to participate fully in the evening’s rituals, but Sam needed me now, in a way that couldn’t wait. My heart pounded as I stood in the hallway, torn between the pull of family duty and the urgent plea of a friend in crisis.
